paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches me: God's promises don't depend on how well anybody is listening. The Israelites are so crushed that "they did not listen to him" (Exodus 6:9). Moses is so nervous that he says twice that he is "unskilled in speech" (Exodus 6:12, 6:30). And through all of it, God keeps right on saying "I will" (Exodus 6:6-8).

Look at what God leans on when Moses is shaking. He says, "I have heard the groaning of the Israelites… and I have remembered My covenant" (Exodus 6:5). He doesn't answer Moses' worry by making Moses a better talker. He tells Moses what He Himself will do, and He says Pharaoh will not listen to Moses at first (Exodus 7:3-4). So the rescue rests on God's arm, not on Moses' mouth, and that gets me every time.

So baker, when you feel too tired, too nervous or too stuck to do what God asks, remember this. Moses is no hero here until he simply does it: "Moses and Aaron did just as the LORD had commanded them" (Exodus 7:6). You don't have to feel ready. You just have to say yes, and trust the One who remembers His promises. I said yes from the back of a drawer, and I'm still baking, so TRUST me on this one!
